issues.description: The return type of Stock.take(String) is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement's UML and the solution implementation define take(String) to return int (returning -1 on failure, remaining quantity on success), but the template's Stock.take(String) returns boolean. This prevents students from implementing the intended logic described in the problem (e.g., checking for -1 to detect failure) and will cause compile/type errors or confusion when following the UML/solution examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template's Stock.take(String) signature and implementation to return an int (like the UML and solution): return -1 when the ingredient is missing or quantity is insufficient, otherwise decrement quantity and return the remaining quantity. This aligns the template with the problem statement and the solution reference.
